_comment: What a fenced block is, and which fences hold a diagram: the one definition every tool reads (diagram audit.py, edit prose_audit.py, publish.py through fences.py; the magazine builder directly). A fence opens with a run of at least minLength of one marker character and closes with a run of the same character at least as long, alone on its line; unterminated, it runs to the end of the document. The info string's first word is the language. A marker with anyLanguage false is a fence only when that language is a diagram language: Azure DevOps writes ::: mermaid, while ::: note is prose. Languages are matched without regard to case.

figureLabels._comment: A diagram's title and caption, in plain markdown so every surface renders them: the title a paragraph of one line, entirely bold, just above the fence; the caption a paragraph of one line, entirely italic, just below. Blank lines between are allowed. The diagram gate requires both; the magazine prints them with the plate.
figureLabels.title: ^[ \t]*(?:\*\*(?!\*)(.+?)\*\*|__(?!_)(.+?)__)[ \t]*$
figureLabels.caption: ^[ \t]*(?:\*(?![*\s])(.+?)\*|_(?![_\s])(.+?)_)[ \t]*$
